tests.name: Effective description
tests.message: Verdict not allowed for this test: 'warning' (allowed: passed, failed)

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and almost entirely domain-specific — Bedrock API quirks, metric names, billing grouping rules, quota codes — with no generic explanations of concepts the agent already knows (e.g., no 'what is cost explorer' filler). It is terse to the point of being hard to read, but every sentence carries project-specific information.
tests.evidence: 'Usage types vary (-mantle-, -standard, -flex, -priority, -cross-region-global): match a model's lines loosely.' — this is non-obvious domain detail, not generic explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (quota codes, metric thresholds, check definitions, alarm specifics) are all pushed into references/ files, with the body only containing condensed rules, a router table, and a procedure checklist that links out for details.
tests.evidence: 'Detection rules, remediations, citations: cost-analysis.md ... checks-model-invocation.md ...' shows detail is delegated, not embedded.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All seven reference files (api-quirks.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, cost-analysis.md, metrics-and-logs.md, quota-codes.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.
tests.evidence: '[collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md)', '[quota-codes.md](references/quota-codes.md)', '[cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md](references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md)' all appear with proper markdown link syntax.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by specific triggering conditions (which step, which check-id, or which API quirk) telling the agent when to load it.
tests.evidence: 'Load when the step says so: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding); ... [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) (before interpreting a response; quota lookup §18, Step 6);'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (read-only guardrails, labeling billed vs estimated, quota lookup order) are given exact prescriptive steps, while judgment-based tasks (deciding severity context, scoping) explain the why/behavior rather than micromanaging.
tests.evidence: 'Read-only. Never create, resize or delete Provisioned Throughput, never change a quota. Give the exact CLI or IaC and let the user run it.' is prescriptive for a fragile/dangerous action, while 'Ambiguous scope: ask, or use the current region and say so' gives flexibility.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple sources or approaches exist (e.g., pricing source), the skill gives a clear priority order rather than listing equal choices.
tests.evidence: 'Rates, in order: the user (say so); pricing:GetProducts ... or the pricing page read with verify_aws_claim.' establishes a default/fallback order.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (Steps 1–8) for any capacity/cost review, with a router table mapping question types to generic read patterns rather than hardcoded one-off answers.
tests.evidence: 'Run the steps in order... Step 1: Scope... Step 2: Tokens... Step 3: Cost model...' demonstrates a reusable procedure applicable to many cost-review requests.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section cataloguing non-obvious pitfalls and misconceptions specific to Bedrock billing/metrics.
tests.evidence: '"A us. profile bills as us-east-1." It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region' is a concrete gotcha correcting a likely mistake.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides a report template asset for full reports, matching its reviews/report-generation purpose.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the template is stored in assets/ and referenced rather than inlined.
tests.evidence: Body only references '[capacity-cost-report-template.md](assets/capacity-cost-report-template.md)' without reproducing template content inline.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The sole asset file, capacity-cost-report-template.md, is referenced in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies it should be used when assembling a full report, giving a clear condition for loading.
tests.evidence: 'capacity-cost-report-template.md (only for a full report)' and 'A full report follows [capacity-cost-report-template.md](assets/capacity-cost-report-template.md).'

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset link uses a relative path format consistent with skill root structure.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow (Procedure — Capacity & Cost Review) is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: **Scope:**' ... '- [ ] Step 8: Assemble the findings, then run "Before You Present".' confirms checkbox + Step N format throughout.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation checklist ('Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output') instructing the agent to check its own output for errors before presenting.
tests.evidence: 'A confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so.' followed by checklist items like 'Every dollar figure says (billed) or (estimated)...'
